name: 5m Donchian breakout
tagline: A 55-bar QQQ 5-minute breakout, gated by the daily 165-day SMA regime, held in TQQQ until the regime turns off.
summary: A minute-timeframe adaptation of the Turtle/Donchian breakout. The 55-bar channel supplies the entry trigger; the daily QQQ > 165-day SMA regime supplies the exit and the bear-market filter. The book is 100% TQQQ while long and 100% BIL otherwise, with next-bar-open fills and 1 bp costs.
decision_process: Every 5-minute bar, compute the highest high of the prior 55 bars (current bar excluded). If flat, the regime is on, and QQQ closes above that channel, target 100% TQQQ; the order fills at the next 5-minute open. If long and the daily regime is off, target 100% BIL, also filled at the next open. The 15:55 bar is the last bar of the session; its close is the 16:00 print and its target fills at the next session's 09:30 open. No Donchian exit, ATR stop, time exit, or session exit is used in the primary.
rules: Universe and bars: adjusted QQQ/TQQQ/BIL 1-minute data, regular session only, resampled to 5 minutes (78 bars/day), 500 calendar days of warmup.
Entry channel: upper[i] = max(QQQ high over the 55 bars before i); the current bar is excluded.
Regime: QQQ daily close > its 165-day SMA. At the 15:55 bar use the regime through today; at all other bars use the regime through the prior day.
Entry: if flat and regime on and QQQ 5m close > upper, target 100% TQQQ; fill at the next bar's open.
Exit: if long and regime off, target 100% BIL; fill at the next bar's open. No other exit in the primary.
Costs and constraints: 1 bp per fill (5 bp sensitivity), 2% band, long-only, weights sum to 1; BIL earns the T-bill return when out.
verdict: Passes vs TQQQ on both windows (10y 46.36%/59.79%, 5y 37.46%/40.82%) and survives 5 bp, but it is not a strict improvement over the daily baseline: it gains about 1-3 pp of CAGR and gives up about 1-4 pp of max drawdown. Classic Donchian exits on minute bars fail; the daily regime exit is the only robust exit tested.

sources.idea: Buy a break of the prior N-bar high; System 2 uses 55 bars; exit on the opposite 20-bar low; initial stop at 2N.
sources.source: Original Turtles / The Original Turtle Trading Rules (2003)
sources.evidence: System 1: 20-day breakout, 10-day exit; System 2: 55-day breakout, 20-day exit; a breakout is the high or low of the preceding N days; stops at 2N. The 55-bar lookback is the Turtle System 2 parameter mapped to 5-minute bars. The 20/10 and 55/20 exits were tested on 5-minute bars and rejected.

sources.evidence: Quotes StockCharts: 'Price Channels are based on prices prior to the current period.' Used to implement upper[i] = max(high[i-N:i]), current bar excluded.

sources.idea: Range = max(HH-LC, HC-LL) over the prior N days; buy above open + k*range; the opposite band is the exit/reversal.
sources.evidence: Used to implement the long-only Dual Thrust variant (prior-day range, k=0.3/0.5). The swing version passed vs TQQQ (48.40%/49.88% 10y; 34.18%/40.82% 5y); the day-trade version failed (6.74%/6.21%).

sources.idea: The 165-day SMA daily regime, TQQQ/BIL book, next-bar-open fills, 1 bp default, and the pass/fail benchmark.
sources.evidence: research/README.md defines the daily baseline (QQQ > 165-day SMA -> 100% TQQQ, else BIL) and the TQQQ benchmark (39.28%/81.68% 10y; 13.47%/81.68% 5y). bt.py defines next-bar-open fills and the 1 bp default. The 165-day SMA is an internal baseline choice; it is not Faber's 10-month SMA and not Gayed & Bilello's 200-day rule.

sources.idea: The 5-minute 55-bar adaptation and the choice of the daily regime as the exit.
sources.evidence: No external source prescribes a 55-bar 5-minute channel; the 55 length is the Turtle System 2 parameter mapped to 5-minute bars. The entry-N plateau (20-200) and the 1-2 bar execution-lag tests are own backtests.

rejected_sources.source: Original Turtle Trading Rules / 20-10 and 55-20 exits
rejected_sources.why_rejected: Tested as minute exits: Turtle 20/10 = 4.28%/40.38% 10y with 10,183 fills; 55/20 = 17.11%/40.85% with 4,999 fills. Both fail CAGR vs TQQQ; the exit sells the first pullback and re-enters higher.

rejected_sources.source: Own test / intraday 165-day SMA breach exit
rejected_sources.why_rejected: Exit when QQQ trades below the last known 165-day SMA intraday: 44.67%/56.39% 10y, 29.56%/43.78% 5y. Worse than the close-based regime and more whipsaw.
Flat at 15:55: 6.74%/34.19% 10y, 6.21%/24.16% 5y; fails CAGR. Overnight exposure is essential for TQQQ.
-3.56%/62.39% 10y, -0.20%/50.71% 5y. TQQQ's return is overwhelmingly overnight, so a pure intraday version destroys the edge.

rejected_sources.source: Own test / 3x 5m ATR initial stop and 5-day time exit
rejected_sources.why_rejected: 3x ATR stop: 49.00%/48.51% 10y but 32.70%/40.82% 5y. 5-day time exit: 32.30%/58.75% 10y, 21.18%/42.96% 5y. Neither is robust across both windows.

corrections: The web catalog attributes Faber (2007) 'A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation' and Gayed & Bilello (2016) 'Leverage for the Long Run' to this strategy. My report does not use either. The 165-day SMA regime is the internal daily baseline from research/README.md; it is not Faber's 10-month SMA (~200 days) or Gayed & Bilello's 200-day rule. Remove those two papers or mark them 'project-level context, not used here.'

The markdown Verdict says 'One variant passes the stated goal against TQQQ on both windows'; that is wrong. Three variants pass: the primary (46.36%/59.79% 10y; 37.46%/40.82% 5y), Dual Thrust swing k=0.3 (48.40%/49.88%; 34.18%/40.82%) and k=0.5 (45.34%/50.81%; 30.18%/42.44%). The primary is the recommended balance; the page should say 'Three variants pass' or list all three.

The web catalog's decision text says 'Each session the strategy evaluates these checks'; the strategy evaluates every 5-minute bar. The daily regime is updated at the 15:55 bar (close) and filled at the next session's 09:30 open. Correct the cadence.

The web catalog's verdict mentions only the 10y drawdown being higher than the baseline; the 5y drawdown is also higher (40.82% vs 36.86%). Say 'both windows' drawdowns are slightly higher than the daily baseline.'

The catalog's originalturtles.org/rules.htm URL is not in my report and may be dead. The report cites the PDF at therobusttrader.com and the Trading Blox mirror; use those verified URLs and drop the originalturtles.org entry.
Minor: the markdown says '2022 is the only meaningfully negative calendar year'; 2018 is also negative (-3.32%). It is the only double-digit negative year. Consider that precision fix.

Minor: the markdown says the 5y drawdown is worse 'because the strategy's pre-crash equity peak was higher'; that is an inference, not a measured decomposition. Soften to 'largely because the pre-crash equity peak differed.'
